title: George Hoefer, Max Jones and meeting Indians in Paris
summary: He corresponded with jazz writers and in Paris befriended Indian performers including wrestler Sonny Warcloud.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: You were good friends with George Hoefer, the jazz writer. You used to correspond with him. There are some copies of your letters --
Oh, George Hoefer -- he passed away and also I used to correspond with Max Jones at Sinclair Traill --

Of the Melody Maker in London. At one point, I was supposed to have gone to London When I left to go to London I saw an ad in the papers about some Indians in the Champs Elysee theater. So I got homesick for them and I didn't go to London. I went over and hung around with the Indians because they were there. They were a darce group from Montana.
Yeah, yeah. I can't think of their name right now.
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943
So you didn't go to London because of that.
I had the Indians over at the Vieux Columnier with me. I was performing there and they came over.
I see, it was far away from home to find another like member of the group. It was really good.
I went to school with a fellow there, Sonny Chorie and he was a wrestler. He went by the name of Sonny Warcloud.
I think I remember hearing about him.

In all the concert halls that we played all over France, he would be advertised--- "Sonny Warcloud wrestles --" such and such. So I would hope that some day I would run into Sonny because I went to school with him, I know his family, He's from we were very close in Los Angeles, the Mission tribe in California. So one day I was on the Champs Elysee, way across there -- it's a double street, you know -- I hear this big yell, I hear this guy hollering -- "Russell Moore, Russell Moore!" it was Sonny Warcloud.

We got together that evening. Big laugh, big talk about back in the States, we were under the shadows of the Arch d' Triumph.
